table.purpose: Sales transactions carried over from an earlier system: who bought, when, where, how many, at what price, in which currency and with what outcome.
table.grain: One row per legacy sales transaction.
assumptions: The view rpt.v_legacy_transactions exposes this table with business names, so its aliases describe these columns.
unknowns: Whether a transaction can have several lines; the unique f1 suggests one row per transaction.
Which system produced the data and why it stops at 2022-12-30.

columns.name: f1
columns.purpose: Unique number of the legacy transaction.
example_questions: How many legacy transactions are there?

alternatives.purpose: Number of the source document rather than of the transaction.

columns.name: f2
columns.purpose: Code of the customer who made the purchase.

value_domain.description: A letter followed by eight digits.

example_questions: Which customers made the most legacy purchases?
What did customer C00012345 buy before 2023?
assumptions: The code matches the customer code used elsewhere in the database.
unknowns: Which table holds the master record for these codes; there is no declared foreign key.

alternatives.purpose: A card identifier rather than a customer code.

columns.name: f3
columns.purpose: Date of the transaction, stored as a yyyymmdd number.

value_domain.description: Dates between 2019-01-01 and 2022-12-30 as yyyymmdd integers.

example_questions: What were legacy sales per month in 2021?
On which days did sales peak?
assumptions: It is the sales date rather than a posting date.

alternatives.purpose: Date the transaction was booked in accounting.

columns.name: f4
columns.purpose: Time of day of the transaction as an hhmmss number; leading zeros are lost (80000 = 08:00:00).

value_domain.description: Times between 08:00:00 and 21:59:59 stored as integers.

example_questions: At what time of day do most legacy sales happen?
assumptions: Five-digit values are times before 10:00 without the leading zero.
unknowns: Whether the time is local store time.

alternatives.purpose: A running number within the day.

columns.name: f5
columns.purpose: Number of units sold in the transaction.
example_questions: How many units were sold in 2020?

columns.name: f6
columns.purpose: Price of one unit in the transaction currency.
example_questions: What was the average unit price per store?
assumptions: The price is in the currency of f10.

columns.name: f7
columns.purpose: Total value of the transaction: quantity times unit price.
example_questions: What was legacy revenue per year?
Which store had the highest sales amount?
assumptions: No discount or tax is included, since f7 = f5 × f6 exactly.
unknowns: Whether cancelled transactions (f8 = CN) should be excluded from revenue.

columns.name: f8
columns.purpose: Outcome of the transaction: completed, cancelled or returned.
example_questions: What share of legacy transactions were cancelled?
assumptions: OK = completed, CN = cancelled, RT = returned.
unknowns: The exact meaning of each code; a lookup table may define them.

alternatives.purpose: Result of the payment rather than of the sale.

columns.name: f9
columns.purpose: Code of the store where the transaction took place.

value_domain.description: A letter followed by three digits; 140 distinct values.

example_questions: Which store sold the most before 2023?
unknowns: Which table describes the stores; there is no declared foreign key.

columns.name: f10
columns.purpose: ISO 4217 currency of the prices and amount.
example_questions: How much legacy revenue was in US dollars?
